research_question: What is the effect of a single sympathetic nerve block, compared with standard care, on pain score at 14 days?
outcome_description: Pain score at 14 days post-intervention, measured using validated numerical or visual rating scales (e.g., Visual Analogue Scale [VAS], Numeric Rating Scale [NRS]).
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater pain reduction (lower pain score) favoring the sympathetic nerve block group over standard care.
search_queries: sympathetic nerve block standard care pain score trial
sympathetic block controlled trial pain outcome 14 days
stellate ganglion lumbar sympathetic block pain reduction randomized
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies examining patients undergoing a single sympathetic nerve block compared to standard care or control.
Reporting of quantitative pain score outcomes assessed at 14 days (or approximately 2 weeks) follow-up.
Controlled comparative study designs (e.g., randomized controlled trials, non-randomized comparative trials).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No comparison between a sympathetic nerve block group and a standard care or control condition.
No quantitative outcome data on pain score at 14 days that can produce an effect size (means and SDs, medians with IQR, t/F statistics, or change scores required).
Completely unrelated to sympathetic nerve block or pain management.
moderators_to_extract: Specific anatomical block target (e.g., stellate ganglion, lumbar sympathetic chain, celiac plexus)
Underlying clinical indication / pain etiology (e.g., CRPS, neuropathic pain, ischemic pain)
Control condition type (e.g., pharmacotherapy alone, sham injection, active comparator)
Injectate composition (e.g., local anesthetic alone vs. local anesthetic with corticosteroid or adjuvant)
Risk of bias / study design (e.g., RCT vs. non-randomized comparative trial)
effect_size_note: Standardized mean difference (Hedges' g) or mean difference across validated pain assessment scales (e.g., VAS, NRS) measured at 14 days post-intervention.
